stem.en: The boulder at the foot of Girnar hill carries three inscriptions. Put them in the order they were cut, oldest first.

text.en: A long Sanskrit inscription by a Western Satrap ruler, giving his military achievements and recording the repair of the Sudarshana Lake.
Major Rock Edicts in Prakrit and Brahmi, spreading the message of Dhamma and moral governance.
A Gupta emperor's record noting the restoration of the Sudarshana Lake after severe damage.

explanation.en: The Prakrit Major Rock Edicts come from Aśhoka in the 3rd century BCE. The Western Satrap ruler Rudradaman I added his inscription in about 150 CE, and the Gupta emperor Skandagupta added his in the 5th century CE.

hints.en: Dhamma was the message of the Mauryan emperor Aśhoka.
The Guptas came after the Western Satraps.
